q: What is history, as distinguished from the past?
options: The actual events that already happened
A disciplined reconstruction and interpretation of the past using surviving traces
A collection of opinions about the past
explanation: The past is what actually happened. History is the reconstruction of it from evidence, so there can be several histories of one past.

q: What is a primary source?
options: Any source found in a textbook
A source that is always truthful
A summary written by a modern historian
Material created during or near the event, or by people directly connected with it
explanation: A source is primary because of its closeness to the event, not because it is automatically true. It still needs criticism.

q: What does provenance mean when evaluating a document?
options: Where the document came from and whether its chain of custody can be traced
explanation: Provenance asks where the document came from and who kept it. Content asks what the text says.

q: What is corroboration?
options: Checking whether independent sources confirm the same details
explanation: Corroboration is the last element of A-T-P-A-C-C: do independent sources confirm it?

q: In the historical argument formula, what is a counterclaim?
options: Why your evidence supports your claim
explanation: The counterclaim is the strongest opposing view, which you then answer with a rebuttal.

q: Who was the eyewitness chronicler of the Magellan expedition who described the Easter Sunday Mass at Mazaua?
explanation: Pigafetta described Mazaua, the Mass, the local rulers, and the planting of a cross. Albo was the pilot who kept the log.

q: Who was Francisco Albo?
options: A Katipunero who witnessed the Cry
A Jesuit who heard Rizal's confession
The pilot whose log gives route and latitude information for Mazaua
explanation: Albo's pilot log gives navigational data that can be compared with geography to locate Mazaua.

q: Who are GOMBURZA?
options: Fathers Mariano Gomez, Jose Burgos, and Jacinto Zamora
explanation: The three Filipino priests were executed on February 17, 1872 after the Cavite Mutiny and became a symbol of colonial injustice.

q: What is the Cuerpo de Vigilancia material in the Rizal retraction debate?
options: Spanish surveillance records of Rizal's final hours
explanation: These newer surveillance records give another official view of Rizal's last day and can challenge earlier witness accounts.

q: What is the Cry of the Philippine Revolution?
options: The symbolic start of the Revolution against Spain, linked with Bonifacio, the Katipunan, and the tearing of cedulas
explanation: The Cry marks the symbolic beginning of open revolution in August 1896.

q: In A-T-P-A-C-C, what does Purpose ask?
options: Why the source was created, such as to record, persuade, justify, or commemorate
explanation: Purpose is why the source was made. Author is who, Time is when, and Audience is for whom.

q: What does voluntariness mean in the retraction debate?
options: Whether the act was free from pressure
Whether the document was found in 1935
explanation: Even if a document is signed, voluntariness asks whether it was done freely. Authorship asks whether the signature is Rizal's.

q: On what date was the recorded Easter Sunday Mass held in 1521?
explanation: The Mass was held on Easter Sunday, March 31, 1521, at the island the sources call Mazaua.

q: Which site is the current dominant position for the 1521 Easter Sunday Mass?
explanation: Historical panels uphold Limasawa because route, latitude, maps, and geography fit better. Butuan rests mainly on local tradition.

q: When and where did the Cavite Mutiny happen?
options: January 20, 1872, at the Cavite Arsenal (Fort San Felipe)
explanation: The mutiny was on January 20, 1872. February 17, 1872 is the execution of GOMBURZA.

q: Which witness placed the Cry at Pugad Lawin on August 23, 1896?
explanation: Valenzuela's account supports Pugad Lawin, August 23. Masangkay said Balintawak on August 26, and Alvarez said Bahay Toro.

q: Whose testimony is the main Jesuit evidence for the Rizal retraction?
explanation: Fr. Vicente Balaguer's testimony is used by the pro-retraction side. Burgos was one of GOMBURZA.

q: In what year did official commemoration of the Cry shift to August 23 at Pugad Lawin?
explanation: The 1963 shift (Proclamation No. 149) favored Pugad Lawin. 1935 is when the retraction document was reportedly found.

q: What is the correct order of the historical argument formula?
explanation: State the claim, give evidence, explain the reasoning, present the counterclaim, then rebut it.

q: What is the correct order of the A-T-P-A-C-C lens?
options: Audience, Time, Purpose, Author, Context, Corroboration
Author, Time, Purpose, Audience, Context, Corroboration
Author, Text, Proof, Argument, Claim, Conclusion
Time, Author, Context, Purpose, Audience, Corroboration
explanation: A-T-P-A-C-C is Author, Time, Purpose, Audience, Context, Corroboration.

q: For the Cry controversy, what is the best historical practice order?
options: Position first, evidence second, definition third
Evidence first, position second, definition third
Definition first, evidence second, position third
explanation: Define what you mean by the Cry first, because different definitions point to different dates and places.

q: Which sequence of 1872 events is correct?
options: Cavite Mutiny on January 20, then the execution of GOMBURZA on February 17
Execution of GOMBURZA, then the Cavite Mutiny
The Cry, then the Cavite Mutiny
Rizal's execution, then the Cavite Mutiny
explanation: The mutiny on January 20, 1872 was followed by arrests and the execution of GOMBURZA on February 17, 1872.

q: Which is NOT a reason historical controversies happen, according to the lesson?
explanation: The four reasons are incomplete evidence, conflicting witnesses, power and bias, and public memory. Sources are not equally reliable.

q: Which pairing of a historian and an interpretation of the Cavite Mutiny is mismatched?
options: Rafael de Izquierdo: broad separatist conspiracy
T. H. Pardo de Tavera: broad separatist conspiracy
Jose Montero y Vidal: Spanish colonial account
T. H. Pardo de Tavera: localized mutiny over grievances
explanation: Pardo de Tavera gave the Filipino version, a localized mutiny. The conspiracy version came from Izquierdo and Montero y Vidal.

q: Which is NOT evidence used by the pro-retraction side?
options: Different versions of the text that do not match
explanation: Mismatched versions are a question raised by the anti-retraction side.

q: Which pairing of a witness and the place of the Cry is mismatched?
explanation: Santiago Alvarez is associated with Bahay Toro, not Pugad Lawin.

q: Which statement is NOT good historical practice?
options: Weighing the evidence on both sides
Using official recognition or popularity as a substitute for evidence
Acknowledging the limits of a source
explanation: Emotion, nationalism, popularity, and official recognition are not substitutes for evidence.

q: A student says, 'Limasawa is correct because the government says so.' What is wrong with this argument?
options: It has a rebuttal but no claim
It relies on official consensus instead of source-based evidence such as route and geography
explanation: Consensus is not primary evidence. A strong argument explains why the route, latitude, and maps fit Limasawa.

q: A government report from 1872 gives exact dates of the mutiny but also defends harsh punishments. How should a historian treat it?
options: As valuable for its details but limited by its political purpose
As useless because it is biased
As completely true because it is official
explanation: A source can be valuable and limited at the same time. Bias tells the historian what to check, not to throw the source away.

q: Two witnesses name different places for the Cry. What does the lesson say this shows?
options: Witnesses may remember different moments as the Katipuneros moved, and old place names covered different areas
explanation: Multiple place names do not automatically prove lying. Boundaries changed, the Katipuneros moved, and the Cry can be defined differently.
